the anodic microbial diversity is the key to maximize bioenergy recovery from WAS via MFCs.

the F/T liquid and fermentation liquor could both be used as effective feedstock in MFCs to treat sludge, and their anodic microbial consortial diversity and evenness, as well as the abundance of functional genes related to electrogenesis, played important roles in the electricity generation.

the microbial mechanism of electrogenesis in MFCs fed with F/T liquid versus fermentation liquor for sludge management, and it can provide some new understanding for maximizing bioelectricity output via MFCs.

the microbial mechanism associated bioelectricity output from sludge matrix fed MFCs and a novel scheme of cooperative interactions in anode biofilm of MFCs was proposed for exploring microbial consortium toward electrogenesis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MFCs fed with fermentation liquor would be more favorable for bioelectricity production than those with the F/T liquid.

the anodic biofilm community structure of MFCs was mainly influenced by the different anodic microbial consorta of the two feeds and the electrogenesis efficiency was closely related with the abundance of functional genes of anodic biofilm.
the MFCs fed with fermentation liquor could be a promising technology for bioelectricity generation and sludge treatment simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MFC technology can provide a novel way for energy recovery from wastewater sludge, which is of significance to sludge management and wastewater treatment.

the anodic microbial consortium of MFCs fed with F/T liquid exhibited higher abundance and diversity of electrogenic bacteria and higher electrogenesis efficiency than that of fermentation liquor, which might be due to the fact that the former was more favorable for the growth and activity of fermentative microorganisms.

the F/T liquid could be a promising feed to cultivate anodic microbial community with higher power generation and electrogenesis efficiency in MFCs, and the fermentation liquor was a better feed for MFCs to achieve more power generation and higher electrogenesis efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MFC fed with fermentation liquor could achieve better performance in terms of power generation, which could provide new insights into the development of MFC technology for the treatment of wastewater and the generation of electricity.

the microbial mechanism of MFCs fed with sludge matrix of freezing/thawed liquid is different from that of fermentation liquor, while both of the two feeds are capable of producing electricity through the synergistic cooperative interactions between fermentative bacteria and exoelectrogems.
the MFCs fed by F/T liquid and fermentation liquor could be applied for the treatment of WAS and bioelectricity generation.
